proposal.problem_statement: Graph neural networks are widely used for text classification [@wang2024; @rizvi2025]. A 2022 study reported that a wide MLP on bag-of-words outperforms TextGCN and HeteGCN and is comparable with HyperGAT [@galke2022]. Graph-based methods published since then report gains over existing methods [@donabauer2025]. Whether the simple baseline still holds against them, and how stable the comparison is across random seeds, was not established by the literature retrieved for this proposal.
proposal.background: TextGCN builds one graph over words and documents and classifies documents with a GCN [@yao2019]. Later work moved to other graph constructions, including graphs over language-model tokens [@donabauer2025]. Evaluation practice matters: for node classification, different data splits changed which GNN ranked best [@shchur2019]. A closely related comparison exists whose abstract and full text could not be obtained [@abdalla2023]; it must be read before work starts.
proposal.research_question: Under one evaluation protocol with five random seeds, does a wide MLP on bag-of-words reach the test accuracy of a text-graph classifier published after 2022 on short- and long-text benchmarks?

hypothesis.text: On each benchmark, the mean test accuracy of the bag-of-words MLP is within one percentage point of the graph model, or higher.

proposal.falsification: Supported on a dataset if the 95% bootstrap confidence interval of the accuracy difference (graph minus MLP) lies below +1 point. Rejected if the interval lies entirely above +1 point. Inconclusive otherwise; the report then states the interval and stops there.
proposal.project_type: Replication of [@galke2022] (independent rerun with more seeds) followed by an extension (one newer graph model). No new model is proposed.
proposal.dataset: The benchmark files distributed with the TextGCN repository, which the baseline study's README also points to. Only the folder's reachability was checked; file contents, sizes and licence must be confirmed on download. One verified short-text mirror is listed for a sanity check, but its splits may differ from the benchmark version, so it cannot be compared with published numbers.
methodology: Stage 1 (replication): run the public bag-of-words MLP code on the benchmark datasets with five seeds and compare with the numbers published in [@galke2022].
Stage 2 (extension): run one graph model published after 2022 with public code under the same splits, tuning budget and seeds.

methodology.text: TokenGraph is the planned graph model because its repository URL responds; whether the code runs was not checked.

methodology: A logistic regression on TF-IDF features is added as the simplest reference point.
proposal.variables: Independent: model family (logistic regression, bag-of-words MLP, graph model) and random seed. Dependent: test accuracy and macro-F1, training time, peak memory. Controlled: data splits, preprocessing, vocabulary, hyperparameter search budget per model, hardware.
confounds: Unequal tuning: give every model the same number of validation-set trials.
Transductive graph models see test documents (without labels) during training; state for each model whether it is transductive or inductive and compare within the same setting where possible.
Fit vocabulary and TF-IDF statistics on training data only; never tune on the test split.
Pretrained language-model embeddings give the graph model external knowledge the bag-of-words model lacks; report this as a difference in resources, not only in architecture.
baselines: Published numbers from [@galke2022] and [@donabauer2025] for reference
metrics: Test accuracy (confirm in the full texts that this is the measure the compared papers report)
Macro-F1, in case classes are imbalanced
Wall-clock training time and peak memory
procedure: Week 1: obtain and read [@abdalla2023] and the full text of [@galke2022] and [@donabauer2025]; stop and reframe if the comparison already exists.
Week 2: set up both codebases with pinned environments; confirm the data files and their licence.
Week 3: Stage 1 runs with five seeds; compare with published numbers.
Weeks 4-5: Stage 2 runs under the shared protocol.
proposal.statistics: Report mean and standard deviation over five seeds for every model and dataset. Compare models with a paired bootstrap on test predictions (10,000 resamples) giving a 95% confidence interval for the accuracy difference. With several datasets, report every interval rather than selecting the favourable ones.

feasibility.text: About six weeks of an eight-week budget
The MLP runs on CPU; the graph model needs a GPU for language-model embeddings and should fit in 8 GB for short texts
No hardware requirement is stated by either repository

contribution.text: An independent, multi-seed check of a published result that questions a line of work, plus one updated comparison. Either outcome is informative.

risks.text: The comparison may already be published in [@abdalla2023] or elsewhere; novelty confidence is low. Fallback: report Stage 1 alone as a reproduction.
The graph model's code may not run or may exceed 8 GB. Fallback: a different post-2022 graph model with public code, or short-text datasets only.
Benchmark data licence is not stated by any API.

limitations: Background summaries rest on abstracts; full texts were not read when this proposal was drafted.
No code was run. Time and hardware figures are estimates.
Semantic Scholar search was unavailable, so prior work may have been missed.
